text: A hospital cannot use equipment that is still waiting for
procurement review. Across Africa, public procurement averages
seventeen percent of GDP, according to the World Bank.
In Zambia, Quorum starts with the officer's desk:
read the evidence, identify the gaps, and prepare a decision
that people can explain.
Here is the actual supplier workflow.
Required documents stay together in one checklist.
The supplier opens a supporting file and requests an AI document
check. The findings appear beside the source, so the reviewer
can compare them. This helps prepare the submission;
it does not decide whether the supplier qualifies.
Now the recorded officer workspace.
The team moves from the tender notice through opening and
evaluation. Published criteria govern the review.
Officers can inspect the matrix, compare the admitted bids, and
trace the supporting file.
These earlier recordings use illustrative records;
their fields vary. The committee enters its own scores.
Quorum keeps the review and the accountable decision connected.
The officer opens the AI-assisted bid review,
confirms permission to share the documents, and starts the
assessment. Every admitted bidder is considered against the same
issued criteria. Watch what happens when the submitted
information does not establish a requirement:
the result says, not evidenced.
The AI leaves the gap visible and gives the committee questions
to resolve. It can offer an advisory comparison, but it cannot
turn missing evidence into a pass.
Muse Spark on Meta Model API also returned the separately
verified source-linked assessment included with this submission.
The original recording also shows the people who make the
decision. Here is the committee panel, followed by member
registration. Each officer has an identity, role and recorded
position. Evaluator sheets, score differences and committee
consensus remain part of the file.
The AI's recommendation is advice for consideration;
official scores, formal ranking and the award remain with
authorised people. Quorum keeps that distinction visible.
We also tested the approval boundary against the production
build. An unsigned request returns four oh one.
A signed-in request without step-up verification returns four oh
three. The gate remains pending with no receipt.
A separate authorised fictional account then completes
two-factor verification, and the local simulation produces a
signature-verified receipt. This is test evidence, not a
government portal transaction.
Quorum. Built by Chungu Chama.
The agent prepares the file.
The authorised committee makes the decision.
